headline: Cybersecurity Surge Can't Mask Monday's Bruises as Bond Yields and Geopolitics Cloud the Open
body_html:
Futures traders are navigating a cautious pre-market Tuesday after Monday's sharply split session left 281 names in our 545-stock universe in the red against 263 advancers. The day's defining tension remains intact: a blistering rally in cybersecurity and software names coexists with severe damage in semiconductors, which shed 6.59% as a sector — the worst reading across the board — while Materials fell 2.48% and Energy dropped 1.88%. That divergence is the first thing to watch at the open.

The macro backdrop has grown more complex overnight. U.S. ten-year Treasury yields have climbed to their highest level since 2007, a development that typically pressures growth-oriented equities and raises the cost of capital across the board. A fresh CNBC survey cements expectations for at least two additional Federal Reserve rate increases over the coming year, and Fed governor Kevin Warsh is reported to face a difficult confirmation path as the central bank braces for its next move. Both data points argue for continued volatility in rate-sensitive pockets of the market.

Geopolitical risk is the third variable. Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic has thinned materially after a new round of Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, even as Riyadh's civil-defence authorities declared the immediate danger past in several cities including Yanbu. Disruption to cloud infrastructure in the Gulf — with at least one major data zone offline — adds a technology-supply dimension that warrants attention as the session gets under way.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity Names Dominate Monday's Leaderboard
briefs.body: A broad wave of buying swept through security software on Monday, with Zscaler surging 16.52%, Qualys climbing 15.06%, CrowdStrike advancing 13.85%, and Palo Alto Networks gaining 13.09%. Okta added 11.98%. The cluster move suggests institutional rotation into the sub-sector rather than isolated, stock-specific catalysts.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Posts Steepest Sector Decline of the Session
briefs.body: The semiconductor space shed 6.59% on Monday, dragged lower by Corning off 13.7%, Teradyne down 13.3%, MaxLinear falling 13.12%, Coherent losing 12.73%, Semtech dropping 12.07%, and Advanced Energy declining 11.45%. The breadth of the selloff points to sector-wide pressure rather than individual earnings disappointments.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Touch Highest Mark in Nearly Two Decades
briefs.body: U.S. ten-year yields rose to their loftiest level since 2007 overnight, intensifying pressure on equities with stretched valuations. The bond market move follows mounting evidence that the Federal Reserve's tightening cycle has further to run, with a closely watched survey now calling for at least two additional rate hikes over the next twelve months.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Shipping Disruption Deepens as Houthi Strikes Restart
briefs.body: Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has thinned significantly after Houthi forces renewed strikes on Saudi targets and negotiations over passage rights stalled. Energy traders are watching closely, as prolonged disruption to one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints could amplify the volatility already evident in the Energy sector, which fell 1.88% on Monday.

briefs.headline: Gulf Cloud Infrastructure Hit by War Damage, Outage Lingers
briefs.body: A major cloud-services data zone in Bahrain and one in the UAE remain inaccessible following damage tied to regional conflict, according to reports citing infrastructure sources. The outage underscores the physical vulnerability of digital supply chains to Middle East instability and may factor into enterprise technology spending conversations in coming weeks.

briefs.headline: Fed Confirmation Fight Adds Policy Uncertainty Ahead of Rate Decision
briefs.body: Kevin Warsh is reported to face a steep climb toward confirmation as the Federal Reserve prepares for an expected interest-rate increase. The contested process injects an element of institutional uncertainty at a moment when markets are already pricing additional tightening, potentially complicating forward guidance and communication from the central bank.
